prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
System: Alder Creek Electrical Distribution Substation, supplying distribution circuits via transformer and feeder bays. Automation boundary: bay monitoring/control, station coordination, external interfaces; primary equipment, protection, field wiring stay within approved designs.

Elements:
- Bay Automation Controller (Juniper): bay sequencing, status, permissives; produces Bay Status Digest; requests Breaker Control Unit operations only when mode/permissives allow.
- North Bay Controller, South Bay Controller.
- Feeder Protection Relay (Tandem): local feeder protection independent of supervisory availability; approved setting group defines pickups, delays, logic; produces Relay Diagnostic Note.
- Breaker Control Unit: executes authorized operations; enforces local interlocks.
- Station Supervisory Control System (Glasswing): operator interface, no protection; produces Alarm Acknowledgement Slip.
- Station Gateway: authorized external comms boundary.
- Satellite Time Receiver (Bluefin): distributes time; produces Clock Drift Snapshot on offset condition; time-quality synchronized/degraded/unavailable.
- Sequence Event Archive; Maintenance Remote Terminal (no local authority); Station DC System (control power).
- Engineering Workstation: holds working and approved configuration plus revision history under revision control; access limited to assigned engineering personnel; produces Settings Review Receipt after settings review.

Actors:
- Control Room Operator: directs operation; confirms indications after comms recovery; coordinates access with Switching Desk Coordinator before work affecting energized equipment.
- Protection Relay Engineer (Larkspur): develops changes against approved protection study/equipment data; documents basis/effect; verifies coordination objectives; records approval status before release.
- Second qualified reviewer: independently checks calculations, logic, applicability.
- Substation Field Crew (Cinder): inspections, maintenance, switching support within approved work; follows work instructions in setting transfer; access only after authorization/site entry controls.
- Substation Supervisor: ensures authorization process; escalates availability concerns.

Requirements:
- Local control precedes remote; interlocks authoritative; protection trips independent of control.
- Settings change: unique revision ID before review; review confirms completeness/consistency; coordination upstream/downstream over operating range; no approval from copied values; pre-deployment check vs device model/firmware; outage/work window if protection affected; post-install compare and functional check; any discrepancy stops release until resolved/reviewed.
- Comms loss may stale displays; timestamps don't validate decisions; holdover degrades; station power loss interrupts visibility/time.

New part:
S078: The Substation Supervisor confirms that the requested work is consistent with current operating conditions and approved procedures.
S079: The crew reviews the work scope, access route, known hazards, and communication arrangements before entering the yard.
S080: Personnel use the site access process to record arrival and departure so that the control room can account for field staff.
S081: Work boundaries are established before tools or test equipment are brought near electrical apparatus.
S082: The Switching Desk Coordinator confirms the applicable switching and clearance arrangements before work begins.
S083: The Control Room Operator retains authority to suspend work when operating conditions change or indications become uncertain.
S084: The Substation Field Crew verifies equipment identity at the point of work against the approved work documentation.
S085: Field personnel do not rely on screen indications alone to establish that equipment is safe to approach or handle.
S086: Required checks of position, isolation, and absence of hazardous energy are performed using approved site procedures.
S087: Any discrepancy between field observations and control-room indications is treated as an unsafe condition until resolved.
S088: The crew promptly reports uncertain equipment conditions through the designated operational communication channel.
S089: Substation Field Crew completes and sends the Breaker Inspection Tag after recording the observed breaker condition and inspection time.
S090: The Station Supervisory Control System presents available equipment indications for operator review during normal operation.
S091: The Bay Automation Controller applies configured permissives and interlocks to supported automated operations.
S092: Automation does not replace field verification when a procedure requires direct confirmation of equipment condition.
S093: The Control Room Operator evaluates reported field conditions before authorizing a return to automated operation.
S094: Field crews maintain communications with the control room throughout work that could affect protection, control, or service continuity.
S095: If communications are lost, the crew stops affected work and follows the approved hold and escalation procedure.
S096: Work is considered complete only after personnel, tools, and temporary connections are accounted for and the work area is left in a safe state.
S097: The Switching Desk Coordinator confirms the operational handback arrangements before equipment is returned to service.
S098: The Sequence Event Archive is the station's authoritative repository for time-stamped operational event evidence.
S099: The Sequence Event Archive is known operationally as Orchard.
S100: It preserves event records in their received form so later review does not depend on transient operator displays.
S101: Each retained record includes its source identity, event time, archive receipt time, and available quality indications.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
